To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have modified pseudorabies virus to express reporter proteins, (2) the expression kinetics of the reporter genes are IE, (3) the reporter genes are co-expressed with neuronal mRNA, and (4) the modified pseudorabies viruses are suitable for tracing central autonomic circuitry in rats.

the Bartha pseudorabies virus has been modified to express the lacZ or GFP reporter gene in neurons infected by the virus and that the reporter gene expression is restricted to the early stage of infection.

(i) we modified the pseudorabies virus Bartha by insertion of the lacZ and GFP genes into the P(LAT2) promoter; (ii) the modified viruses labeled central auton- omy in a slower and more restricted manner than Bartha; and (iii) both lacZ and GFP expression kinetics were controlled by the IE1 promoter and allowed co-labeling with mRNA in tyrosine hydroxylase and serotonin transporter expressing neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of pseudorabies viruses that can be used to study the neurochemical and functional organization of central nervous system circuitry.
the generation of recombinant PRV strains that are useful for labeling and neuroanatomical characterization of central nervous system circuitry.
the construction of a novel pseudorabies virus-based trans-synaptic tracer, which is suitable for the co-determination of reporter gene products with neuronal mRNas in infected neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed two novel recombinant pseudoviruses, which can be utilized to label and characterize neural circuitry in a more detailed manner than previously possible.
the modified Bartha virus strains are suitable tools for tracing neuronal circuitry and for the detection of mRNA expression in the same cell.
the new viruses are excellent tools for the labeling and neurochemical analysis of neural circuitry in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have created a set of pseudorabies viruses that are optimized for labeling and co-detection of neurochemical phenotypes in neurons.
Bartha virus mutants with disrupted LAT2 promoter function are suitable for labeling of central autonomic neurons and for co-detection of neuronal mRNAs and reporter proteins.
the Bartha-derived pseudorabies viruses with IE reporter gene expression are suitable for tracing of neural circuitry and for the co-detecting of neuronal mRNAs in the same cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
recombinant pseudoviruses expressing the lacZ or GFP genes can be used to study the connectivity of neurons expressing tyrosine hydroxylase and serotonin transporter.
pseudorabies virus can be modified to label neural circuits in a more restricted fashion and to allow the co-labeling of reporter proteins with cellular transcripts.
the modified Bartha viruses are useful tools for the neurochemical characterization of trans-synaptic neural circuits.
